acceptance: Replay of the 1691 shape: a correction re-dispatch whose agent fixes a non-deliverable file and leaves a well-formed deliverable untouched completes without operator action.
A correction re-dispatch where the agent changes NOTHING still does not complete on the stale deliverable (the cycle-1550 guard holds).
A first dispatch still refuses a pre-dispatch leftover deliverable.
Host-made writes (challenge token, telemetry, .evolve/ state) never count as evidence that the agent acted.
Read-only phases (audit, adversarial-review) never qualify: their stale verdict completes only by being rewritten after dispatch.
The bridge REPORTS the evidence (a worktree snapshot at dispatch vs at idle); core runs `phase verify` — the bridge does not import phase verifiers.
The correction directive asks for an appended `## Correction N` section (pinned in the correction-prompt composition).

consumed.resolution: A correction of a source-writing phase now asks the bridge for the worktree-evidence completion contract (core.PhaseRequest.BridgeCompletion, projected by the runner): at an idle checkpoint the bridge completes on the unrewritten pre-dispatch deliverable when a git-status worktree snapshot changed since dispatch on a non-host path, reports it (note + BRIDGE_COMPLETED_ON_WORKTREE_EVIDENCE), and core verifies as usual; every correction directive now asks for an appended ## Correction N section (ADR-0113, go/internal/bridge/completion_worktree.go).

fix: Keep the guard for every dispatch. Add a deterministic second path for a carried-forward deliverable: for a correction re-dispatch of a SOURCE-writing phase, the host completes the phase when the agent goes idle with the deliverable present and well-formed AND the worktree changed since the correction dispatch through the AGENT's own edits. Promote the correction-prompt instruction into the protocol: the correction directive asks the agent to append a `## Correction N` section to the deliverable recording what it fixed (works up front — 1691 lost ~20 min between the fix at 04:39 and the nudge reply at 04:58).
notes: Console-owned by kind (the fix surface is the protected bridge + orchestrator). Evidence: runs/cycle-1691 (build-report.md mtime 04:37:45 < correction dispatch 04:37:58; the builder pane at 04:58 said 'Phase is complete'); operator touch 05:16:07 recorded in the campaign memory. Frequency risk: every build-floor correction whose fix is an explanation doc or source-only change. | 2026-09-26: PART 1 landed (fix/correction-completion-nudge): the idle nudge names an unrewritten deliverable and why a rewrite is needed (bridge.nudgeMessage). PART 2 REMAINS: deterministic completion for a correction re-dispatch whose worktree changed and whose deliverable verifies.
priority_rationale: inbox review 2026-09-27: Evidenced inside the window: the 1707 build idled about 20 minutes, 1691 needed an operator touch, and six more recoveries in 1706-1720 depended on the one-shot nudge. An agent that declines the nudge turns a correct cycle into an exit-81 FAIL, a process block the P0 policy says must be recovered.
root_cause: The stale-leftover guard (cycle-1550: never accept a pre-dispatch artifact as this attempt's result) is right for EVERY dispatch — its founding case was itself a correction re-dispatch. What is missing is a second, honest evidence source for a deliverable legitimately CARRIED FORWARD: a correction whose fix lives in another file leaves the previous attempt's accurate deliverable untouched, and nothing asks the agent to re-check and re-affirm it (part 1, the explaining nudge, now does).
summary: Cycle 1691 (wave 8, 2026-09-26): the build handoff floor rejected the build (one Changed Areas path needed a what/why line in the explanation doc) and correction 1/2 re-dispatched at 04:37:58. The builder fixed the explanation doc at 04:39 — correctly: build-report.md needed no change and `evolve phase verify build` reported it well-formed. But the bridge's completion check (completion.go artifactBaseline: size+mtime of the deliverable captured at dispatch) requires the deliverable to CHANGE after dispatch, so it treated the phase as incomplete, sent the one-shot nudge ('Please write the deliverable…'), and the agent — correctly seeing the report was already right — re-verified and answered 'Phase is complete' without rewriting. The phase sat idle until the operator touched build-report.md at 05:16 (content unchanged, verified) — otherwise the stop-review would have closed it as exit 81 and failed a correct cycle on a pipeline defect.
title: F39 part 2: a correction round whose fix lives outside the deliverable must complete deterministically (part 1, the explaining nudge, has landed)
